expert_decode: D2H compact sorted top-10 expert ids from rank 0
mmap one exact checkpoint expert on each miss
pack the exact full-K BFP4 gate/up and down matrices on expert_id % 2 and exact zeros on the non-owner
H2D only missed owner/zero expert pairs through fixed per-rank staging
local D2D copy into fixed generation-checked slots
expert_prefill: D2H compact unique routed expert ids
bounded waves of at most 10 experts
each gate-selected expert executes once for its wave
ple: CPU EOS-aware n-gram hash with isolated two-token request history
mmap only selected BF16 table rows
H2D exact assembled [batch, sequence, 2560] rows into stable staging
PLE projection, gating, convolution, recurrence, and residual stay on TT
forbidden: Torch PLE projection or decoder math
host lookup or H2D inside trace capture

expert_cache.packed_host_zero_storage: one shared exact-zero BFP4 rank shard per layer; cached experts retain only their exact owner shard
expert_cache.parallelism: EP2 deterministic owner expert_id % 2; shared expert remains TP2
expert_cache.replacement: stable indexed generation-checked LRU slots for traced decode; deterministic generation-checked LRU waves for prefill
expert_cache.trace_index_contract: a persistent replicated uint16 slot-index row changes router order without relocating hit expert weights; the back trace consumes stable slot addresses
expert_cache.failure_semantics: publish a generation only after both ranks and projections upload; invalidate the slot on any failure

ple_table.lookup_contract: torch.unique deduplicates each exact batched request, then per-shard index_select gathers only misses from safetensors mmap handles
ple_table.chunk_contract: 128 logical rows per device prefill staging wave; public non-aligned tails are padded, masked, and sliced internally
ple_table.pinned_host_staging: unavailable in torch 2.11.0+cpu on this host; contiguous CPU rows are handed to TT runtime staging

measured_limitations: Exact demand-loaded prefill is substantially slower than resident optimized prefill because a large routed-expert union is serviced in bounded waves.
Token decode does not speed up on TP2 after exact host service, canonical-state DRAM movement, gathers, and one or two fixed collectives are included.
Host-backed decode is batch one; the resident optimized multichip path retains the validated batch-32 contract.
